claims.title: The Yenisei Kyrgyz destroy the Uyghur Khaganate
claims.summary: The Yenisei Kyrgyz overthrew the Uyghur Khaganate and sacked its capital Ordu-Baliq, briefly making the Kyrgyz the dominant power of the eastern steppe and driving the Uyghurs out of Mongolia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kyrgyzstan: From the Yenisei steppe and the epic of Manas to a turbulent mountain democracy.", terralore.co/country/KGZ/chronicle#ev-840-the-yenisei-kyrgyz-destroy-the-uyghur-khaganate, claim TL:KGZ:event:840:the-yenisei-kyrgyz-destroy-the-uyghur-khaganate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Transmission of the epic of Manas
claims.summary: The Kyrgyz preserved the vast oral epic of Manas, recited by bards (manaschi), telling of the legendary hero who united the Kyrgyz tribes; it remains the cornerstone of Kyrgyz cultural memory.

sources.label: Kyrgyz epic trilogy: Manas, Semetey, Seytek

claims.title: Manas trilogy recognized by UNESCO
claims.summary: UNESCO inscribed the Kyrgyz epic trilogy of Manas, Semetey and Seytek on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, recognizing one of the world's longest oral epics.

sources.label: Kyrgyz epic trilogy: Manas, Semetey, Seytek

claims.title: Karakhanid Balasagun and the Burana tower
claims.summary: Under the Karakhanid dynasty, the first Turkic Muslim power in Central Asia, Balasagun in the Chüy valley flourished as a capital; its minaret, the Burana tower, survives as the best-known monument of northern Kyrgyzstan.

sources.label: Kyrgyzstan: Silk Roads Programme (Burana and the Chüy valley)

claims.title: Mongol conquest of Central Asia
claims.summary: The empire of Genghis Khan overran Central Asia, drawing the Kyrgyz lands into the Mongol world and, after the empire's division, into the Chagatai realm and its successor states.

sources.label: Kyrgyzstan: A Country Study (in Kazakstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan: Country Studies)

claims.title: Kyrgyz consolidate in the Tian Shan
claims.summary: Through the upheavals of the post-Mongol centuries the Kyrgyz tribes settled in the Tian Shan, living as mountain nomads organized in tribes and clans, the homeland they hold to this day.

sources.label: Kyrgyzstan: A Country Study (in Kazakstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan: Country Studies)
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: Sulaiman-Too inscribed by UNESCO
claims.summary: The sacred mountain of Sulaiman-Too above Osh, with its petroglyphs, places of worship and reconstructed 16th-century mosques, became Kyrgyzstan's first UNESCO World Heritage Site, recognized for its blend of pre-Islamic and Islamic belief.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kyrgyzstan: From the Yenisei steppe and the epic of Manas to a turbulent mountain democracy.", terralore.co/country/KGZ/chronicle#ev-2009-sulaiman-too-inscribed-by-unesco, claim TL:KGZ:event:2009:sulaiman-too-inscribed-by-unesco, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kyrgyz under the Khanate of Kokand
claims.summary: The Khanate of Kokand extended its rule over the Kyrgyz tribes, building the fortress of Pishpek (later Bishkek) to control the Chüy valley and recruiting Kyrgyz fighters, though its rule was widely resisted.

sources.label: Kyrgyzstan: A Country Study (in Kazakstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan: Country Studies)
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: Russia annexes Kokand; Kyrgyzstan under imperial rule
claims.summary: After suppressing an uprising, the Russian Empire abolished the Khanate of Kokand and annexed its lands as the Fergana Province, bringing the Kyrgyz country under direct Russian colonial rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kyrgyzstan: From the Yenisei steppe and the epic of Manas to a turbulent mountain democracy.", terralore.co/country/KGZ/chronicle#ev-1876-russia-annexes-kokand-kyrgyzstan-under-imperial, claim TL:KGZ:event:1876:russia-annexes-kokand-kyrgyzstan-under-imperial, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The 1916 revolt (Urkun)
claims.summary: A decree conscripting Central Asians for wartime labour triggered a revolt across Russian Turkestan; in the Kyrgyz lands it was suppressed with great violence, and tens of thousands fled toward China, with heavy loss of life. Casualty figures remain estimates.

sources.label: Kyrgyzstan: A Country Study (in Kazakstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan: Country Studies)
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: Kara-Kyrgyz Autonomous Oblast created
claims.summary: In the Soviet national-territorial delimitation of Central Asia, the Kyrgyz lands were organized as the Kara-Kyrgyz Autonomous Oblast within the Russian SFSR, giving the Kyrgyz their own named territory for the first time.

sources.label: Kyrgyzstan: A Country Study (in Kazakstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan: Country Studies)
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: The Kirghiz SSR becomes a union republic
claims.summary: Kyrgyzstan was elevated to the Kirghiz Soviet Socialist Republic, a full constituent republic of the Soviet Union, with its capital at Frunze (formerly Pishpek, today Bishkek).

sources.label: Kyrgyzstan: A Country Study (in Kazakstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan: Country Studies)

claims.title: Chingiz Aitmatov wins the Lenin Prize
claims.summary: The Kyrgyz writer Chingiz Aitmatov was awarded the Lenin Prize for 'Tales of the Mountains and Steppes', bringing Kyrgyz literature to a worldwide audience and becoming the republic's most celebrated cultural figure.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kyrgyzstan: From the Yenisei steppe and the epic of Manas to a turbulent mountain democracy.", terralore.co/country/KGZ/chronicle#ev-1963-chingiz-aitmatov-wins-the-lenin-prize, claim TL:KGZ:event:1963:chingiz-aitmatov-wins-the-lenin-prize, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Akayev chosen to lead the republic
claims.summary: Amid Gorbachev's reforms and rising ethnic tension in the south, the physicist Askar Akayev was elected head of the Kirghiz SSR, the leader who would guide the republic to independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kyrgyzstan: From the Yenisei steppe and the epic of Manas to a turbulent mountain democracy.", terralore.co/country/KGZ/chronicle#ev-1990-akayev-chosen-to-lead-the-republic, claim TL:KGZ:event:1990:akayev-chosen-to-lead-the-republic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kyrgyzstan declares independence
claims.summary: As the Soviet Union collapsed, the Supreme Soviet of the republic declared Kyrgyzstan's independence; Askar Akayev became the first president of the sovereign state, with its capital at Bishkek.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kyrgyzstan: From the Yenisei steppe and the epic of Manas to a turbulent mountain democracy.", terralore.co/country/KGZ/chronicle#ev-1991-kyrgyzstan-declares-independence, claim TL:KGZ:event:1991:kyrgyzstan-declares-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: U.S. recognition and diplomatic relations
claims.summary: The United States established diplomatic relations with independent Kyrgyzstan on 25 December 1991, opening its embassy in Bishkek in February 1992 as the Soviet Union was dissolved.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations, by Country: Kyrgyzstan
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: The Tulip Revolution
claims.summary: Allegations of fraud in the parliamentary elections and of pervasive corruption sparked mass demonstrations that forced President Akayev to flee the country, in the first of Kyrgyzstan's post-Soviet revolutions.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kyrgyzstan: From the Yenisei steppe and the epic of Manas to a turbulent mountain democracy.", terralore.co/country/KGZ/chronicle#ev-2005-the-tulip-revolution, claim TL:KGZ:event:2005:the-tulip-revolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The 2010 revolution ousts Bakiyev
claims.summary: A violent uprising in Bishkek over corruption and rising prices forced President Kurmanbek Bakiyev to flee; an interim government under Roza Otunbayeva took power and prepared a new constitution.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kyrgyzstan: From the Yenisei steppe and the epic of Manas to a turbulent mountain democracy.", terralore.co/country/KGZ/chronicle#ev-2010-the-2010-revolution-ousts-bakiyev, claim TL:KGZ:event:2010:the-2010-revolution-ousts-bakiyev, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ethnic violence in the south
claims.summary: Clashes between ethnic Kyrgyz and Uzbeks in Osh and Jalal-Abad erupted into days of communal violence, killing several hundred people — figures are estimates and remain contested — and displacing hundreds of thousands.

sources.label: 'Where is the Justice?': Interethnic Violence in Southern Kyrgyzstan and its Aftermath

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kyrgyzstan: From the Yenisei steppe and the epic of Manas to a turbulent mountain democracy.", terralore.co/country/KGZ/chronicle#ev-2010-ethnic-violence-in-the-south, claim TL:KGZ:event:2010:ethnic-violence-in-the-south, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Parliamentary republic and the first peaceful transfer
claims.summary: A new constitution made Kyrgyzstan a parliamentary republic, a rarity in Central Asia; the 2011 election that followed Otunbayeva's interim presidency was the country's first peaceful handover of power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Kyrgyzstan: From the Yenisei steppe and the epic of Manas to a turbulent mountain democracy.", terralore.co/country/KGZ/chronicle#ev-2010-parliamentary-republic-and-the-first-peaceful, claim TL:KGZ:event:2010:parliamentary-republic-and-the-first-peaceful, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Japarov and the return to presidential rule
claims.summary: After 2020 protests over disputed elections, Sadyr Japarov rose from prison to the presidency, winning election in January 2021; constitutional referendums then restored a strong presidential system.

sources.label: Kyrgyzstan: In Brief (Sadyr Japarov and the 2021 constitutional changes)
